prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1313; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling eastbound in the left-hand lane of a multi-lane arterial in Houston, Texas, and was turning left at the intersection when the collision occurred. Driver 2 was proceeding westbound and struck the front driver's side of the vehicle operated by Driver 1. Driver 1 reported that a passenger was seated in the front right position at the time of impact. I arrived on scene and confirmed the presence of that passenger, and the statements gathered from the parties at the scene were consistent on this point. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated on scene before being transported for further care. The described injuries are consistent with the mechanism of a side impact of this type. Damage to the vehicle, including the deformed front driver's side panel and displaced wheel assembly, matches the impact described by all parties. Scene photographs taken by officers corroborate several of the details provided, although no independent witnesses came forward. Records available to me show no prior damage to the vehicle in this area.
